narrative:
The model predicted an 88.2% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is so high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Being in the bottom decile of your class that year signaled much weaker performance than the typical student who is admitted. Your first-year ranking in the second decile added further weight in the same direction, showing that your grades started below the level of most successful applicants.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.5 worked in your favor, as it sits noticeably above the average of accepted students. However, this positive signal was not strong enough to offset the two low class rankings.

Taken together, the model saw your consistently lower class standing as the dominant indicator that you were unlikely to pass the bar on the first try, which led directly to the rejection.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record and bar-exam readiness. Consider retaking key courses to raise your class rank, enrolling in a structured bar-preparation program, or gaining additional legal experience before reapplying. These steps can demonstrate improved readiness and improve your chances in a future cycle. (218 words)
